# Creality Pika pocket 3D scanner with up to 0\.03mm accuracy, marker-free scanning launched ⓘ CrealityCreality Pika 3D scanner is a pocket-sized device\. Creality has launched the Pika 3D scanner, which is just 100x60x35mm in size\. While it doesn’t come with the post-processing capabilities of the Sermoon P1, there is a screen for an easier scanning experience\. After the Sermoon S1, X1, and the all-in-one P1, Creality has now launched the Pika, a significantly more compact 3D scanner\. Of course, it is not as accurate or performant as its bigger siblings, but the built-in screen and portable nature of it are what set it apart from the competition\. And it is still highly accurate\. ## Creality Pika features and specifications The Pika 3D scanner measures 100x60x35mm and weighs just 260 grams\. It offers two scanning modes: parallel blue laser \(seven lines\) and NIR\. It is capable of scanning accurately up to 0\.03mm with the former and 0\.1mm with the latter\. There is a 3-inch HD touchscreen with 500 nits peak brightness, but the Pika does not have the standalone power to post-process\. # Creality Pika 3D Scanner Launches with 0\.03 Mm Accuracy The new Creality Pika 3D Scanner offers a compact and precise solution for capturing detailed 3D models across a variety of applications\. Measuring just 100 x 60 x 35 mm and weighing 260 grams, this pocket-sized device combines portability with advanced features like **markerless scanning** and a dual-light system that handles challenging surfaces such as metallic or dark materials\. Its AI-powered capabilities, including **AI Body Completion** and **AI Hole Filling**, further enhance the scanning process by automating tasks that typically require manual adjustments\. With an accuracy of up to 0\.03 mm, the Pika stands out as a practical choice for professionals and hobbyists seeking reliable results in prototyping, part repair, or artistic projects\. # Creality’s Pika Wants To Make 3D Scanning Feel As Easy As Taking A Photo 3D scanning has long been a tedious endeavour, with even simpler options on the market feeling like they require users to learn a complex new skill\. Creality is looking to change that with its new Pika portable 3D scanner\. Designed for portability, the Creality Pika resembles a standard point-and-shoot camera more than the complex equipment many users are accustomed to\. It appears to be a major step forward for makers, creators and anyone interested in 3D printing or modelling\. The company claims the compact device combines traditional 3D scanning with 3D Gaussian Splatting, a rendering technique designed to preserve colour, texture and depth that may be lost in a standard mesh model\. Weighing 260 grams and measuring 100 by 60 by 35 millimetres, the Pika has the profile of a small digital camera, complete with a three-inch touchscreen for monitoring scans\. Creality describes it as “the world’s first smartphone-like portable AI scanner,” reflecting the company’s broader effort to make 3D capture more approachable for hobbyists and professional creators\.
